newsitem.title: CHINA: China paper warns of rising domestic debt.
newsitem.headline: China paper warns of rising domestic debt.

text.p: China's issue of domestic bonds in 1997 is likely to greatly exceed that of 1996, and by some standards this year's amount has broken a limit, the Business News said on Tuesday.
The 1996 issue of domestic bonds is 195.2 billion yuan, of which 133.2 billion will be used to pay back bonds that mature this year, the newspaper said in a front-page analysis.
Official predictions say that the 1997 issue will be substantially higher than that in 1996, with shorter maturities and lower interest rates, it said.
The analysis listed three international standards, which can be used to measure whether China has issued too much domestic debt.
According to one of those standards, the nation's bond issue for this year has breached a limit.

That standard measures whether debt issued in any one year accounts for more than 20 percent of national budgetary expenditure. In China's case, the proportion rose from 19.65 percent in 1994 to 21.75 percent in 1995, and then to 24.68 percent in 1996, exceeding the danger limit, the newspaper said.
However, the country's debt issuance for the year remains within the comfort zone outlined by the other two standards.

One measures whether the annual issue is lower than three percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP), the analysis said. In the case of China, the figure was 2.53 percent in 1994, 2.57 percent in 1995 and 2.85 percent in 1996, it noted.

The other assesses whether the outstanding debt accounts for more than 50 percent of national GDP in any given year. In the case of China, it was 5.1 percent in 1994 and about six percent in 1995 and 1996, the newspaper said.
The analysis warned that the nation's issuance of domestic debt will grow, in line with economic reform and development, and "we must prevent this from resulting in a bad outcome".
